RealtimeVoice wraps the GPT Realtime 2 API into a production-ready platform so you skip the heavy lifting: no WebSocket plumbing, no token budgeting, no session state management. items.description: GPT Realtime 2 bills at $32 per million audio input tokens and $64 per million audio output tokens. Without proper session management, costs can spiral fast. RealtimeVoice gives you per-session cost tracking, automatic token limits, and a built-in cost calculator so you always know what each conversation costs before you scale. Set hard spending caps per user or per session — no surprises on your OpenAI bill.

faq.title: GPT Realtime 2 Questions Answered
faq.description: Everything you need to know before building with GPT Realtime 2 on RealtimeVoice.

items.title: What is GPT Realtime 2?
items.description: GPT Realtime 2 is OpenAI's latest speech-to-speech model released in May 2026. It is the first realtime voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning, supporting a 128K context window, five levels of adjustable reasoning effort, parallel tool calls, and interruption recovery. It is available through OpenAI's Realtime API via WebRTC, WebSocket, and SIP.

items.title: How much does GPT Realtime 2 cost?
items.description: GPT Realtime 2 is priced at $32 per million audio input tokens and $64 per million audio output tokens, with $0.40 per million for cached input tokens. A typical 5-minute conversation uses roughly 5,000–8,000 output tokens, costing around $0.32–$0.51 in API fees. RealtimeVoice's cost calculator helps you model this before you commit.

items.title: Do I need my own OpenAI API key?
items.description: Yes. RealtimeVoice connects to your own OpenAI account so you retain full control over your API usage and billing. We never proxy your traffic through our own OpenAI key — your data stays between your application and OpenAI directly.

items.title: How is GPT Realtime 2 different from GPT Realtime 1.5?
items.description: GPT Realtime 2 adds GPT-5-class reasoning, expands the context window from 32K to 128K tokens, introduces adjustable reasoning effort (minimal to xhigh), supports parallel tool calls with spoken feedback, and delivers 15.2% higher scores on Big Bench Audio benchmarks. For production voice agents, the improvement in instruction following and tool reliability is substantial.

items.title: What use cases work best with GPT Realtime 2?
items.description: GPT Realtime 2 excels at contact center automation, appointment booking, field service support, language learning, healthcare intake, and any workflow where speaking is faster than typing and the agent needs to take real actions mid-call. It is less suited for simple FAQ bots where a cheaper transcription-only model would suffice.

items.title: Can GPT Realtime 2 handle phone calls?
items.description: Yes. GPT Realtime 2 supports SIP connections natively, enabling inbound and outbound telephony. RealtimeVoice provides phone number provisioning and SIP trunk configuration so you can deploy a GPT Realtime 2 agent on a real phone line without managing your own telephony infrastructure.

items.title: What languages does GPT Realtime 2 support?
items.description: GPT Realtime 2 handles multilingual conversations natively. The companion GPT Realtime Translate model supports live speech translation from 70+ input languages into 13 output languages. RealtimeVoice supports both models depending on whether you need a conversational agent or a live interpreter.

items.title: How quickly can I get a GPT Realtime 2 agent live?
items.description: Most users have a working GPT Realtime 2 agent running within 10 minutes of signing up. A production deployment with custom tools and phone integration typically takes 1–2 days. RealtimeVoice provides starter templates for common use cases so you are not starting from a blank prompt.
